summary: Indranil Dutta is a linguist who studied under Hans Henrich Hock. He held a post at the English and Foreign Languages University (attested 2020).

Ines Konczak-Nagel works in history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. Her posts include Berlin State Museums, Ryukoku University (2012), the Saxon Academy of Sciences and Humanities, and the University of Leipzig (attested 2026).
Ingmar Heise works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned an MA in Chinese Studies from Leiden University by 2005 and was attested as a PhD candidate at the University of Bristol in 2012.

Ingo Strauch, a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies, earned his PhD at the Free University of Berlin in 2000. He held posts at the Free University of Berlin (attested 2008), Lausanne (2012), and Washington (attested 2015).
Inyoung Chung is a scholar of Buddhist studies who completed a PhD at the University of Virginia under the doctoral supervision of Paul Groner (attested 2008).

Ioan Mihălcescu (1874–1948) was an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Bucharest, Humboldt University of Berlin, and the University of Leipzig (PhD 1901–1904), and became a Privatdozent at Bucharest in 1904.

Ioan Petru Culianu (1950–1991) worked in religious studies and history/archaeology. Educated at Bucharest, Sacred Heart, Paris-Sorbonne, and under Mircea Eliade, he held posts at the University of Groningen (1976–1986) and University of Chicago Divinity School (1986–1991).
Iona Macgregor is an Indology and linguistics researcher who studied at the University of Hamburg and served there as a Wissenschaftliche Projektmitarbeiterin (attested 2026).
Ippei Okamoto is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He held posts at Toyo University (attested 2014) and Minobusan University (attested 2026).

Irach Jehangir Sorabji Taraporewala (1884–1956) worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Indology, and linguistics. He studied under Julius Jolly (~1911–1913) and held posts at Deccan College (~1939–1942) and the Linguistic Society of India (attested 1955).

Iravatham Mahadevan (1930–2018) was an Indologist, archaeologist, and linguist. He studied at Jaffna College and the University of Madras (~1949–1953) under mentor Murray Barnson Emeneau, founded the Roja Muthiah Research Library, and worked at Dinamani (1987–1991).

Irawati Karve (1905–1970) worked in Indology and history/archaeology. She studied at Fergusson College, Huzurpaga, and the University of Mumbai under Govind Sadashiv Ghurye, later serving as professor at Deccan College (~1939–1970) and visiting the University of Pennsylvania (~1959–1960).

Irfan Habib (born 1931) is a historian and Indologist. He studied at Minto Circle, Aligarh Muslim University (~1947–1953), and New College (~1954–1958), and served as a historian at Aligarh Muslim University from around 1953 to 1991.

Irina Anatolyevna Svetovidova (1930–1968) was an Indologist who studied at Saint Petersburg State University (~1950–1955). She worked as a researcher at the Leningrad Oriental Institute (1957–1968) and taught at Saint Petersburg State University (1965–1968).
Irma Piovano is an Indologist who studied under mentor Oscar Botto. She served as supervisor of scientific activities and cultural relations at CESMEO (attested 2005–2008).

Irving Babbitt (1865–1933) was a scholar of philosophy who studied at Harvard, EPHE, and the University of Paris. He taught Romance languages at Williams College (1893–1894) and served as an assistant professor at Harvard University (1894–1912).

Isaac Schapera (1905–2003) studied at Cape Town, Cándido Candi, and the London School of Economics under Bronisław Malinowski. He worked in history and archaeology, holding posts at the University of Chicago (~1948), Toronto, and LSE (~1950–1969).

Isaak Jakob Schmidt (1779–1847) was a scholar in Tibetology, Central Asian, and Buddhist studies who earned a doctorate at Rostock (~1826). He held posts at the Russian Bible Society, Saint Petersburg State University, and the Russian Academy of Sciences.

Isabelle Henrion-Dourcy is a Tibetologist who earned PhDs from EPHE and ULB, studying under Fernand Meyer and Françoise Lauwaert. She completed postdoctoral work at Harvard and was appointed Full Professor at Laval University in 2007.

Isabelle Onians is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. She earned her PhD from the University of Oxford by 2002 and served as an editor at the Clay Sanskrit Library (attested 2007).
